finding.observation: In rmcp-v3.1.4 TaskManager::cancel_task, cancellation of a nonterminal task sets cancel_requested=true, signals cancel_signal, clears pending_inputs, touches the task and recomputes status before returning. Because current_status is InputRequired only while pending_inputs is nonempty, cancellation removes the old input_required exposure immediately; before terminal settlement the observable status is Working. Dropping the pending oneshot senders makes parked TaskContext::request_input awaits resolve with TaskExit::Cancelled. The exact cancel_wakes_parked_input_requests test waits for InputRequired, cancels, verifies the parked await is woken, and then observes Cancelled after the operation propagates that error. update_task removes only currently pending keys, so responses for cleared/superseded keys are ignored while the task still exists.
finding.scope_limit: The test does not guarantee that an immediate tasks/get after cancel must visibly return Working because the operation may race to a terminal state. What is source-guaranteed for a nonterminal entry at cancel_task return is that the old pending input set has been cleared; therefore the pre-cancel InputRequired payload cannot remain authoritative. Cancellation remains cooperative: an operation may catch the cancellation-derived error and later complete or fail instead of settling Cancelled.
finding.persistent_restart_rule: For an application-owned persistent task store, acknowledge cancellation only after durably recording cancel_requested for the stable task identity and atomically invalidating/clearing the currently pending input set (while retaining lifetime-used input keys or an equivalent anti-reuse fence). Every restart claim/redrive and tasks/get must consult that durable cancellation/input state; stale tasks/update responses for invalidated keys must not revive or satisfy old waits. A generation/CAS fence should prevent a pre-cancel attempt from re-publishing superseded pending input after the acknowledgement. Do not force terminal Cancelled merely from the acknowledgement; preserve operation-defined cooperative settlement semantics.
finding.why_it_matters: This closes the pending-input cleanup subproblem left by revision 88: cancellation acknowledgement is not only a cancel-intent fence, it also establishes an input-supersession boundary that persistent restart logic must preserve. It does not solve external-effect exactly-once safety or stock TaskManager restart durability.
